aspect: You may not know who employs you
description: Workers relying on intermediaries often do not know their actual Israeli employer. The intermediary collects wages directly and deducts fees before passing on the remainder.
energy_note: Can't sue them. Don't know their name.

aspect: Off the books means no rights accrue
description: Kav LaOved documents workers paid off the books, denying them social rights, sick pay and holidays, plus unlawful dismissals. Years of work produce no pension entitlement and no injury cover.
money_note: Unaccrued social rights over a working life.
energy_note: Thirty years of work, no pension record.

aspect: An injury ends the income permanently
description: An undocumented worker injured on an Israeli site has no accident cover, cannot easily prove the employment relationship, and loses the permit along with the ability to work.
energy_note: Hurt at work, and instantly unemployed and uninsured.

aspect: EXAMPLE - the Bank of Israel's own estimate
description: The Bank of Israel put broker profits at NIS 122 million in 2018, the year in which 45% of the 94,254 Palestinian workers in Israel obtained their jobs through agents who could take up to a third of a worker's wages. The central bank of the state operating the permit system measured the market the system created.
energy_note: A hundred and twenty-two million shekels, measured by the central bank.
